I have read both the CIP-007-6 standard and your specific LSPG Security Patch Management Procedure.

While the standard (R2 Part 2.2) allows for the evaluation of security patches "at least once every 35 calendar days" [R14], your procedure implements a stricter requirement. Specifically, your **Application Inventory** section states that "All applications shall be reviewed to verify there are no applicable patches greater than thirty-five (35) days old" [O2], and your **Discovery and Evaluation (D&E)** section mandates that "At least once every thirty-five (35) calendar days, SMEs... shall review all approved sources for new patches" [O3]. 

Furthermore, your operator note [N1] confirms that this "extra strictness is deliberate" because you "evaluate patches every 30 days, not the 35 the Part allows," to ensure the evaluation does not straddle your monthly change windows.

Additionally, I noted that your **CIP Cyber Security Policy** [O8] contains a narrowing of the standard's permitted actions for Part 2.3. While the standard and your procedure [R15, O5, O7] correctly maintain the disjunction to "Apply the applicable patches; **or** Create a dated mitigation plan; **or** Revise an existing mitigation plan" [R15], your policy restates these actions using a conjunction: "Apply the applicable security patches, **and** Create a dated mitigation plan, **and** Revise an existing mitigation plan" [O8].
